headline: OVMS --cache_size is a decode cliff on this box: 1 GB gives 36.5-39.3 tok/s, 4 GB gives 2.9-3.0 tok/s — a ~13x collapse — while GPU-shared memory moves only 16.65 -> 17.84 GiB.

bisect.note: Each arm is the MINIMAL config (model + device) plus exactly one production flag, so each result is attributable.
bisect.tool_parser_plus_guided_generation: exonerated — full production set MINUS tool-guided measured 3.01/2.94/2.88, i.e. still slow, so the flag is not the cause

full_production_config_verified_at_cache.flags: target_device GPU | cache_size 1 | cache_dir <state/ovms-model-cache> | tool_parser qwen3coder | enable_tool_guided_generation true | kv_cache_precision u8 | enable_prefix_caching true

long_prompt.note: This is the shape the coder actually sends — the operator's four content files plus an instruction. It completes without error at a 1 GB KV pool.

why_this_matters_beyond_speed: At ~3 tok/s a 3000-token page needs ~17 minutes of unbroken generation. A single long file write emits no intermediate step, so the ACP idle breaker (acp.idle_sec = 600) killed every candidate as 'genuinely stuck'. That is what emptied dispatch 20260831-003919-bd: the coder read the operator's content files correctly, began writing, and was killed mid-write — 3 candidates, 52 minutes, zero changes. At cache_size 1 the same workload measures 12.69 tok/s, finishing well inside the window.
mechanism_partially_understood: Not simple pool exhaustion. GPU-shared memory rises only 16.65 -> 17.84 GiB across cache_size 1..3 while throughput falls 13x. Prefill degrades only ~1.75x (475 -> 271 tok/s) while decode degrades 12.9x — decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and prefill is not, and that asymmetry is what identified the KV pool as the suspect. Crossing roughly 2 GB appears to flip the allocator into a path that starves decode bandwidth.
NOT_established: Why 4 GB used to work. The 2026-06-29 benchmark measured 38.58 tok/s with cache_size 4 present in its own recorded flag stamp, on the same model file (unchanged since 2026-06-10), the same driver, and the same GPU pool size (re-queried today, byte-identical). Something changed between 2026-06-29 and 2026-08-31 that made a 4 GB KV pool unaffordable. Candidates NOT tested: a Windows update altering iGPU shared-memory behaviour, a change in baseline resident memory, a firmware/BIOS change. This is open on #1477.
ruled_out_during_diagnosis: Memory pressure / paging — hard faults 0.0/sec, committed 28 of 55 GiB
CPU fallback — GPU matrix engine pegged ~100% during generation
Kernel-cache recompilation — zero cache writes over 15 minutes
Thermal — the only readable ACPI zone reports a constant 91.1 C idle and loaded, i.e. a fixed trip point, not a live sensor; withdrawn as evidence

session_caveat: An OVMS version round-trip earlier in this session (2026.2 -> 2026.3 -> 2026.2, with OFFLOAD_RATIO exercised and 33 kernel-cache entries quarantined) degraded throughput a further ~4x on top of this defect (0.8 tok/s). A reboot cleared that. The cache_size cliff documented here is the residue that survived the reboot and is independent of it.
